title: IELTS Speaking Test 21
description: Part 1: School days, Teachers, Learning now. Part 2: Describe a teacher who influenced your education. Part 3: two-way discussion.

part1.intro: Good morning / afternoon. Can you tell me your full name, please? What can I call you? Where are you from? Can I see your identification, please? Thank you.

questions: Did you enjoy your time at school?
Which subjects were you best at?
Did you have a favourite teacher?
What is your strongest memory from school?
What qualities make a good teacher?
Do you prefer strict teachers or relaxed ones?
Have any teachers changed the way you think?
Is teaching a respected profession in your country?
Are you still learning new things?
How do you prefer to learn as an adult?
Do you think people learn better when they are young?
What would you like to learn next?

part2.cueCardTitle: Describe a teacher who influenced your education.
points: and explain how they influenced you.
roundingOff: Are you still in contact with this teacher?
Would you like to thank them?

questions: What makes a teacher truly memorable?
Do you think the role of teachers is changing?
How important is the relationship between a teacher and a student?
Should teachers focus more on exam results or on developing character?
Do you think technology could ever replace teachers?
How could the teaching profession be made more attractive?

title: IELTS Speaking Test 22
description: Part 1: Your country, News and events, Leadership. Part 2: Describe a leader you admire. Part 3: two-way discussion.

part1.intro: Good morning / afternoon. Could you tell me your full name, please? What can I call you? Where do you come from? May I see your identification? Thank you.

questions: What do you like most about your country?
What is it well known for?
Has your country changed much recently?
What would you show a visitor first?
How do you keep up with current events?
Do you follow national or international news more?
Do you discuss the news with others?
Do you think the news affects people’s opinions strongly?
Do you consider yourself a leader?
Have you ever led a group or a team?
What do you think makes a good leader?
Would you like to be in a position of leadership?

points: what they are or were responsible for
and explain why you admire them as a leader.
roundingOff: Would you like to lead in the way they do?
Do many people admire this person?

questions: What are the most important qualities of a good leader?
Are leaders born or made, in your opinion?
Do you think good leaders always need to be popular?
How much influence do leaders really have on people’s lives?
Should young people be encouraged to develop leadership skills?
What can happen when a country has poor leadership?

title: IELTS Speaking Test 23
description: Part 1: Music, Talent, Performances and shows. Part 2: Describe a talented person you know, such as a musician, an artist or an athlete. Part 3: two-way discussion.

part1.intro: Good morning / afternoon. Can you tell me your full name, please? What can I call you? Where are you from? Can I see your identification, please? Thank you.

questions: Do you enjoy listening to music?
What kind of music do you like best?
Do you play any instruments?
Is music important in your culture?
Do you think you have any special talents?
Is it better to have one talent or many skills?
Do you admire talented people?
Can talent be developed, or is it natural?
Do you enjoy going to concerts or live shows?
Have you ever performed in front of others?
Do you prefer live performances or recordings?
Are performances popular in your country?

part2.cueCardTitle: Describe a talented person you know, such as a musician, an artist or an athlete.
points: and explain why you think they are so talented.
roundingOff: Do you think they will become well known?
Would you like to have their talent?

questions: Do you think talent is more important than practice?
Why are some people talented in many areas?
Should schools do more to identify and support talented students?
How can society best support gifted young people?
Do you think talented people always achieve success?
Is it possible for anyone to become talented at something?

title: IELTS Speaking Test 24
description: Part 1: Where you live, Neighbours, Community. Part 2: Describe a neighbour you get along with well. Part 3: two-way discussion.

part1.intro: Good morning / afternoon. Could you tell me your full name, please? What can I call you? Where do you come from? May I see your identification? Thank you.

questions: What kind of area do you live in?
Do you know the people living near you?
Is it a quiet or a busy neighbourhood?
Would you like to live somewhere different?
Do you get on well with your neighbours?
What makes someone a good neighbour?
Do neighbours help each other where you live?
Have neighbours become less friendly over time?
Are there community events where you live?
Do you feel part of your local community?
What could bring your community closer together?
Is a sense of community important to you?

part2.cueCardTitle: Describe a neighbour you get along with well.
points: how long you have known them
and explain why you get along with them.
roundingOff: Do you help each other out?
Would you like to have more neighbours like them?

questions: Why is it important to have a good relationship with neighbours?
Do you think people know their neighbours less well than in the past?
What problems can arise between neighbours?
How can neighbours build a stronger sense of community?
Do people in cities and in the countryside treat neighbours differently?
Should local governments do more to bring communities together?

title: IELTS Speaking Test 25
description: Part 1: Relaxing, Noise, Weekends and rest. Part 2: Describe a quiet place you like to go to. Part 3: two-way discussion.

part1.intro: Good morning / afternoon. Can you tell me your full name, please? What can I call you? Where are you from? Can I see your identification, please? Thank you.

questions: What do you do when you want to relax?
Where do you feel most peaceful?
Do you prefer quiet places or lively ones?
Is it easy to find quiet places where you live?
Does noise bother you?
Is the area where you live noisy?
What kinds of noise do you find most annoying?
Do you think cities are becoming noisier?
How do you rest at the weekend?
Do you get enough rest during the week?
Do you prefer to rest at home or somewhere else?
Is rest important for doing well in life?

part2.cueCardTitle: Describe a quiet place you like to go to.
points: and explain why you like this quiet place.
roundingOff: Do you go there alone or with others?
Is it easy to find quiet places these days?

questions: Why do people need quiet places in their lives?
Do you think modern life is too noisy and busy?
How does a noisy environment affect people?
How can cities provide more peaceful spaces for people?
Do you think people appreciate silence enough?
Should there be more rules to control noise in public places?

title: IELTS Speaking Test 26
description: Part 1: Travel and places, Cities, Planning trips. Part 2: Describe a city you would like to visit. Part 3: two-way discussion.

part1.intro: Good morning / afternoon. Could you tell me your full name, please? What can I call you? Where do you come from? May I see your identification? Thank you.

questions: Do you like visiting new places?
What kind of places do you enjoy most?
Do you prefer cities or the countryside?
Where would you most like to travel to?
Do you enjoy spending time in big cities?
What are the advantages of living in a city?
Are there any problems with life in cities?
How have cities in your country changed recently?
Do you enjoy planning trips?
Do you prefer organised tours or independent travel?
How do you decide where to go?
Do you research a place before visiting it?

part2.cueCardTitle: Describe a city you would like to visit.
points: and explain why you would like to visit it.
roundingOff: Do you think you will visit it one day?
Would you go alone or with others?

questions: Why do you think some cities attract so many visitors?
What makes a city a good place to live in?
How can cities cope with growing numbers of tourists?
What are the biggest challenges facing cities today?
Do you think more people will live in cities in the future?
How could cities be made more pleasant places to live?
